questions.prompt: State the Lorentz transformation for \(x'\) when \(S'\) moves at speed \(v\) along \(+x\) relative to \(S\).
questions.answer:
\[
x'=\gamma(x-vt)
\]

questions.prompt: State the Lorentz transformation for \(t'\).
questions.answer:
\[
t'=\gamma\left(t-\frac{vx}{c^2}\right)
\]

questions.prompt: What happens to \(y\) and \(z\) in the standard Lorentz transformation along \(x\)?
questions.answer:
They are unchanged:
\[
y'=y,\qquad z'=z
\]

questions.prompt: In \(S\), an event occurs at \(x=300\,\mathrm m\), \(t=0\). If \(S'\) moves at \(0.600c\), find \(x'\).
In \(S\), an event occurs at \(x=0\), \(t=2.00\,\mu\mathrm s\). If \(S'\) moves at \(0.600c\), find \(t'\).
questions.answer:
With \(x=0\),
\[
t'=\gamma t
\]
Using \(\gamma=1.25\),
\[
t'=2.50\,\mu\mathrm s
\]

questions.prompt: Write the inverse Lorentz transformations for \(x\) and \(t\).
questions.answer:
Reverse the sign of the relative velocity:
\[
x=\gamma(x'+vt')
\]
\[
t=\gamma\left(t'+\frac{vx'}{c^2}\right)
\]

questions.prompt: In \(S\), an event occurs at \(x=900\,\mathrm m\), \(t=4.00\,\mu\mathrm s\). Frame \(S'\) moves at \(0.600c\). Find \(x'\).
For the same event \(x=900\,\mathrm m\), \(t=4.00\,\mu\mathrm s\), and \(v=0.600c\), find \(t'\).
State the relativistic velocity transformation for motion along \(x\).
questions.answer:
If \(S'\) moves at \(+v\) relative to \(S\), then
\[
u_x'=\frac{u_x-v}{1-u_xv/c^2}
\]

questions.prompt: A particle moves at \(0.900c\) in \(S\). Frame \(S'\) moves at \(0.500c\) in the same direction. Find \(u_x'\).
A spaceship fires a probe forward at \(0.700c\) relative to the ship. The ship moves at \(0.600c\) relative to Earth. Find the probe speed relative to Earth.
questions.answer:
Use the inverse velocity transformation:
\[
u_x=\frac{u_x'+v}{1+u_x'v/c^2}
\]
\[
u_x=\frac{0.700c+0.600c}{1+(0.700)(0.600)}=\frac{1.300c}{1.420}=0.915c
\]

questions.prompt: Show that the velocity transformation gives \(u_x'=c\) when \(u_x=c\).
questions.answer:
Substitute \(u_x=c\):
\[
u_x'=\frac{c-v}{1-v/c}=\frac{c(1-v/c)}{1-v/c}=c
\]
So light speed remains \(c\) in the moving inertial frame.

questions.prompt: Two spacecraft approach each other. In Earth frame, one has velocity \(+0.700c\) and the other \(-0.700c\). What speed does one measure for the other?
An event has \(x'=0\) in a frame moving at \(0.800c\). Use the inverse Lorentz transformation to show its path in \(S\).
questions.answer:
The inverse position transformation is
\[
x=\gamma(x'+vt')
\]
If \(x'=0\), then
\[
x=\gamma vt'
\]
The inverse time transformation gives
\[
t=\gamma t'
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{x}{t}=v
\]
so the origin of \(S'\) moves at speed \(v=0.800c\) in \(S\).

questions.prompt: Use the Lorentz transformation to find \(x'\) and \(t'\) for \(x=600\,\mathrm m\), \(t=3.00\,\mu\mathrm s\), and \(v=0.800c\).
Derive the time-difference form of the Lorentz transformation from \(t'=\gamma(t-vx/c^2)\).
questions.answer:
For event 2 and event 1,
\[
t_2'=\gamma\left(t_2-\frac{vx_2}{c^2}\right),\qquad t_1'=\gamma\left(t_1-\frac{vx_1}{c^2}\right)
\]
Subtract:
\[
\Delta t'=t_2'-t_1'=\gamma\left(\Delta t-\frac{v\Delta x}{c^2}\right)
\]

questions.prompt: Show that the Lorentz transformations reduce to Galilean transformations when \(v\ll c\).
questions.answer:
When \(v\ll c\), \(\gamma\approx1\) and \(vx/c^2\) is negligible compared with ordinary times. Therefore
\[
x'=\gamma(x-vt)\approx x-vt
\]
and
\[
t'=\gamma\left(t-\frac{vx}{c^2}\right)\approx t
\]
These are the Galilean position and time transformations.

questions.prompt: Use velocity addition to show that combining two sub-light speeds in the same direction cannot exceed \(c\).
questions.answer:
For \(0<a<c\) and \(0<b<c\), the combined speed is
\[
u=\frac{a+b}{1+ab/c^2}
\]
To compare with \(c\), require
\[
a+b<c\left(1+\frac{ab}{c^2}\right)=c+\frac{ab}{c}
\]
This rearranges to
\[
(c-a)(c-b)>0
\]
which is true. Thus \(u<c\).

questions.prompt: Explain why Lorentz transformations act on events rather than on objects.
questions.answer: A transformation assigns coordinates to a single occurrence with a definite place and time. An extended object requires many events, such as endpoint positions measured at specified times. Confusing objects with events leads to mistakes in length contraction and simultaneity.

questions.prompt: Derive the inverse Lorentz transformation by changing the sign of the relative velocity.
questions.answer:
If \(S'\) moves at \(+v\) relative to \(S\), then \(S\) moves at \(-v\) relative to \(S'\). Starting from
\[
x'=\gamma(x-vt),\qquad t'=\gamma\left(t-\frac{vx}{c^2}\right)
\]
interchange primed and unprimed coordinates and replace \(v\) by \(-v\):
\[
x=\gamma(x'+vt')
\]
\[
t=\gamma\left(t'+\frac{vx'}{c^2}\right)
\]
